Old Timey Mono

Old Timey Mono is a faithful monoline revival of Reproducing Typewriter (1906), a typeface for simulating typewritten copy in advertising brochures, junk mail, etc. It's also the typeface used in the Turbo Pascal 3.0 manual.

Old Timey Code

Old Timey Code is based on Old Timey Mono, and was intended for coding, developing, programming, whatever you call it.

Reproducing Typewriter was developed for simulating typewritten copy in advertising brochures and whatnot, in letters sent to a bulk mailing list, and for other purposes. Shorter serifs and (in some cases) more open arpetures help the typeface survive the imperfections resulting from reproduction, especially at smaller point sizes.

I think those features make it a pretty good typeface for coding, though I had to make additional changes.

Character Coverage

  • Covers almost all Western European languages using Greek, Cyrillic, and Latin scripts.
    • Full support for WGL4, AGLFN, MES-1. (Except ligatures.)
    • Near complete support for W1G, SECS, MES-2.
  • Unicode box drawing, block drawing, braille, IPA, and everything in Code Page 437 (MS-DOS).
  • Additional math symbols and geometric shapes.
  • A few cool surprises.
